## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `604977848d763bc36473bb85a58066de7d8f5a50`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0135-identity-and-access-architecture.md + none (read, not reviewed: PR #33307 at head `ba3fd25ea8`, its `implicit-account-linking.ts`, `sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts` and `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts`; records 6880992920 and 6882064855; `references/security-findings.md` and `lanes/security.md` on `main`)

### ① Derived judgments

- The diff is one file, ADR-0135: a dated note under D6 and one sentence in "What this record does NOT settle". No code, no schema, no published package, no error code. Right.
- The note changes what D6 publishes as the unchanged set: "accounts that already exist are not re-checked" is narrowed to a sign-in that neither links nor changes the stored address. That is a change to a recorded decision (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 13), carried by an amendment to the record on a Tier H path. The vehicle is right; the authority the note names for it is ④ finding 1.
- The rule sentences, read against the first consumer (#33307 at `ba3fd25ea8`): an implicit link judged by the creation rule's own comparison; a sign-in judged only when it would change the stored address; a sign-in that changes nothing not judged; refusal code `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`; the same `user.validateUserInfo` gate. Each agrees with that tree, with the one over-reach in ④ finding 2.
- "What this record does NOT settle": "the D6 notes", plural, now covers both notes. Right.
- The cited path `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/implicit-account-linking.ts` exists on `main`, so the citation resolves in either landing order.
- Check-runs on the head: 49 runs, 26 success, 23 skipped, none failed or pending. Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Documentation Links, Check Changeset and the docs and code guards are green.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` label, no changeset. The diff publishes nothing, so that is the correct level. Clause-②: none declared and none owed; the narrowing itself is declared on #33307, where it ships.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR body: `check:doc-formula-expressions` not measured locally. Answered by the head's check-runs (the docs and code guards lane is green).
- PR body: "lands with or after #33307". Not held by any gate. #33307 is an open draft; if this note lands first, D6 states a rule the tree does not hold. The landing seat holds this PR until #33307 is merged, and re-reads the note if #33307's head moves the rule again.
- Tier H: `docs/adr/**`. Lands by authorised approval only. Because the note amends a recorded decision, that approval is a decision on the rule, not only on prose; the approval ask must say so (see ④ finding 1).
- Author is the fleet bot; no off-relay author to name.

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/adr/0135-identity-and-access-architecture.md` — the rule text is an accurate account of what #33307 implements, and a dated D6 note is the right place for it. It does not hold on who authorises it.

1. must-fix — the authority sentence of the 2026-11-14 note. It names two authorities: the security lane seat's order, and a contract review's reading. Neither can be one. The file's own Status line says nothing is decided in it; the 2026-11-13 note rests the creation rule on the maintainer's ruling "not this file"; D6 on `main` records that existing accounts are not re-checked; and `references/security-findings.md` section 6 sends a fix that sets a contract to the maintainer. A seat's order dispatches work, and a review record reads a rule against the tree; record 6880992920 itself asked for "the ruling that authorises it" and said it could read none. The note as written would put on a governed record that a seat extended a maintainer ruling. Required, one of: (a) if the maintainer has ruled on the extension, the note names that ruling and its date, as the 2026-11-13 note does; or (b) the note says plainly that the extension is decided by the maintainer's approval of this amendment, and the PR's 维护者速读 asks for that decision in those words. In both, record 6880992920 may be cited as the review that required the note, not as authority.
2. should-fix — the summary clause "now holds only for a sign-in that neither links nor changes the stored address". The tree judges an implicit link only; a link the user starts from their own session is not judged (rule 4 in the consumer's header, and #33307's Unchanged list). Say "neither implicitly links", and name the explicit link among what is not judged, so the record's unchanged set matches the tree's.
3. nit — the D6 body paragraph still carries "Accounts that already exist are not re-checked." with no pointer; a reader of the paragraph alone gets the old rule. Add "(see the 2026-11-14 note)" or the like. Prose only.
4. nit — "Both fail closed and answer `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`": the code is what the rule's own refusal answers; an input the gate cannot read is refused by the gate's general refusal. One clause apart would be exact. Prose only.

Finding 1 is a must-fix; findings 1 and 2 earn a delta review of their fix by this seat.
